verdict: Mastercard's net revenue rose 16% to $8.4B as card spending grew around the world, and net income rose 18% to $3.9B — the toll-booth model doing its work again.

segments.name: Payment network
segments.note: Fees every time a Mastercard is swiped, tapped or used online — gross dollar volume was $2.7 trillion in the quarter, up 7% in local currency.

segments.name: Value-added services and solutions
segments.note: Fraud protection, data analytics, consulting and identity services sold on top of the network — growing nearly twice as fast as the network itself.

flow.grossNote: already net of rebates and incentives
flow.grossPlain: Mastercard reports revenue already net of the rebates and incentives it pays banks and merchants to win card business — so there is no separate cost-of-revenue line in its books. The costs were taken out before revenue was counted.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Salaries, technology and offices for the people who run the network — by far Mastercard's biggest cost.

opex.name: Advertising and marketing
opex.note: Brand campaigns, sponsorships and the 'Priceless' advertising.

opex.name: Depreciation and amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of buildings, data centers, equipment and acquired technology.

takeaways.title: Spending held up everywhere
takeaways.text: Net revenue rose 16% (12% currency-neutral). Gross dollar volume grew 7% and cross-border volume 13% on a local-currency basis — travel and everyday spending both contributed.

takeaways.title: Services are the growth engine
takeaways.text: Value-added services and solutions — security, data and authentication tools sold on top of the network — grew 22% to $3.5B, well ahead of the payment network itself (+12%).

takeaways.title: Nearly half of revenue kept
takeaways.text: Net income was $3.9B — 46 cents of every revenue dollar — even after a $202M restructuring charge. Few businesses convert revenue to profit at this rate.

oneTimers: A $202M restructuring charge (inside general and administrative costs) and a $66M loss on equity investments are excluded from Mastercard's adjusted figures; excluding them, adjusted net income was $4.1B and adjusted EPS was $4.60.
otherDetail: Other income (expense) was −$95M: $81M of investment income and $75M of other income, outweighed by $185M of interest expense and a $66M loss on equity investments.
